kings1.18.p1.b1.text: “Go and present yourself to Ahab, and I will send rain upon the face of the earth.”

kings1.18.p1.b2.text: The famine was severe in Samaria,

kings1.18.p1.b3.text: Obadiah had taken a hundred prophets and hidden them, fifty men per cave, providing them with food and water.

kings1.18.p1.b4.text: So they divided the land to explore. Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went the other way by himself.

kings1.18.p2.b2.text: “It is I… Go tell your master, ‘Elijah is here!’”

kings1.18.p2.b3.text: “How have I sinned, that you are handing your servant over to Ahab to put me to death?”

kings1.18.p2.b4.text: “I do not know where the Spirit of the LORD may carry you off when I leave you.”

kings1.18.p3.b1.text: “Was it not reported to my lord what I did when Jezebel slaughtered the prophets of the LORD? I hid a hundred prophets of the LORD, fifty men per cave, and I provided them with food and water.”

kings1.18.p3.b2.text: “As surely as the LORD of Hosts lives, before whom I stand, I will present myself to Ahab today.”

kings1.18.p3.b3.text: So Obadiah went to inform Ahab, who went to meet Elijah.

kings1.18.p4.b1.text: “Is that you, O troubler of Israel?”

kings1.18.p4.b2.text: “I have not troubled Israel… but you and your father’s house have, for you have forsaken the commandments of the LORD and have followed the Baals.”

kings1.18.p4.b3.text: “Now summon all Israel to meet me on Mount Carmel, along with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal…”

kings1.18.p5.b1.text: “How long will you waver between two opinions? If the LORD is God, follow Him. But if Baal is God, follow him.”

kings1.18.p5.b2.text: But the people did not answer a word.

kings1.18.p5.b3.text: “I am the only remaining prophet of the LORD, but Baal has four hundred and fifty prophets.”

kings1.18.p6.b1.text: “Since you are so numerous, choose for yourselves one bull and prepare it first. Then call on the name of your god, but do not light the fire.”

kings1.18.p6.b3.text: But there was no sound, and no one answered as they leaped around the altar they had made.

kings1.18.p6.b5.text: “Shout louder, for he is a god! Perhaps he is deep in thought, or occupied, or on a journey. Perhaps he is sleeping and must be awakened!”

kings1.18.p7.b1.text: So they shouted louder and cut themselves with knives and lances, as was their custom, until the blood gushed over them.

kings1.18.p7.b2.text: Midday passed, and they kept on raving until the time of the evening sacrifice.

kings1.18.p7.b3.text: But there was no response; no one answered, no one paid attention.

kings1.18.p8.b2.text: And Elijah took twelve stones, one for each tribe of the sons of Jacob… And with the stones, Elijah built an altar in the name of the LORD.

kings1.18.p8.b3.text: “Fill four waterpots and pour the water on the offering and on the wood.”

kings1.18.p8.b5.text: So the water ran down around the altar and even filled the trench.

kings1.18.p9.b1.text: At the time of the evening sacrifice, Elijah the prophet approached the altar

kings1.18.p9.b2.text: “O LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, let it be known this day that You are God in Israel…”

kings1.18.p9.b4.text: “…so that this people will know that You, the LORD, are God, and that You have turned their hearts back again.”

kings1.18.p10.b1.text: Then the fire of the LORD fell

kings1.18.p10.b2.text: and consumed the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, and the dust,

kings1.18.p10.b3.text: and it licked up the water in the trench.

kings1.18.p11.b1.text: When all the people saw this, they fell facedown and said,

kings1.18.p11.b2.text: “The LORD, He is God! The LORD, He is God!”

kings1.18.p11.b3.text: “Seize the prophets of Baal! Do not let a single one escape.”

kings1.18.p11.b4.text: Elijah brought them down to the Kishon Valley and slaughtered them there.

kings1.18.p12.b1.text: “Go up, eat and drink, for there is the sound of a heavy rain.”

kings1.18.p12.b2.text: But Elijah climbed to the summit of Carmel, bent down on the ground, and put his face between his knees.

kings1.18.p12.b4.text: “There is a cloud as small as a man’s hand rising from the sea.”

kings1.18.p13.b1.text: Meanwhile, the sky grew dark with clouds and wind, and a heavy rain began to fall.

kings1.18.p13.b2.text: So Ahab rode away and went to Jezreel.

kings1.18.p13.b3.text: And the hand of the LORD came upon Elijah, and he tucked his cloak into his belt and ran ahead of Ahab all the way to Jezreel.
